# NEGATIVE CONTROLS. Every line below is text this repository ALREADY PUBLISHES, taken verbatim
# from a tracked file, and every one of them MUST match no detector. They are checked on every run,
# before anything else is scanned, and a match is exit 2 naming the detector and this line number.
#
# They are here because the cost of this check is not a leak it misses; it is a detector that
# refuses honest work. Each line is one that a slightly broader pattern would have caught: a 64-hex
# digest beside the word `sha256`, a URL with a colon in it, a `key:` with a value, an opam or dune
# stanza, a Rocq `Require`. These lines never supply canary coverage: the canaries in the two
# detector tables are the only evidence that a detector still fires.
#
# A line here is not an exemption. It is a fixture: nothing in a pull request is compared against
# it, and the same text arriving in a change is scanned like any other text -- it simply does not
# match, which is the point.
